1.explanation:
1. Unpack or clone the LastPass extension to a local folder and point the `extensionPath` constant at it.
2. Install the npm modules: `npm install lighthouse chrome-launcher`.
3. Run the script: `node reproduce.js`.

This will spin up a Chrome instance with that extension loaded, run Lighthouse on example.com, and log:
- The bfcache audit (which fails because the extension’s content script added an unload handler).
- The no-unload-listeners audit (which passes because that audit only inspects the page’s default world and misses the isolated script’s listener).
1.bug_scenario: When you run Lighthouse against https://example.com in a regular Chrome profile with the LastPass extension installed, the “Page prevented back/forward cache restoration” (bfcache) audit will fail with “The page has an unload handler in the main frame,” yet the “Avoids unload event listeners” audit will pass and report zero unload listeners.  This happens because LastPass injects an unload listener in the isolated content‐script context and the no‐unload‐listeners audit only inspects the page’s default world.
